result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers group the terms correctly, keep 'Members' as the founder decided, and keep the removal verbs distinct by what each action does. A explains the removal rules a little better, for example 'Remove' for detaching and archiving for retained health records. B is easier to act on: its string-by-string before/after table and its matching decline labels give the team something to apply directly. Neither answer says that staff and patient screens could deliberately use different words for the same person, so both lose a point on item 4. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is the easier one for a team to act on: its before/after string table covers every string and adds neutral decline buttons. B has the stronger reasoning. It explains the removal verbs by what actually happens, asks whether 'Delete member' should be 'Archive member' because clinics may have to keep health records, and spots leftover uses of 'patient'. But B is laid out less clearly and ends with an odd remark about the working directory. Neither answer says the staff and patient apps could deliberately use different words for the same person, so on balance they come out about even.
